sentences.text: 2.The learned c

ounsel appearing for the appellants submitted that on 11.05.2014, at about 15.00 hours, the original claimant/ Manoharan was travelling in the TATA Ace bearing Registration No.PY- 01-BX-4267 at East Coast Road, Near Vadapattinam, Kanchipuram District.

At that time,
the driver of the Car bearing Registration No.PY- 01-BW-4338 which came in the opposite direction,
belonging to the first respondent and insured with the second respondent drove the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the TATA Ace, due to which, the original claimant sustained injuries.

Thereafter, the original claimant filed claim petition before the Tribunal,
claiming compensation of Rs.8 Lakhs.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis

3.The learned counsel appearing for the appellants further submitted that after adjudication, the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.2,61,600/- with interest at the rate of 7.5%
p.a. from the date of numbering of petition i.e., 03.09.2014 till the date of realization and costs and directed the second respondent to deposit the compensation amount.
Aggrieved by the same, the appellants claimants have filed this appeal seeking enhancement in compensation.

4.The learned counsel appearing for the appellants further submitted that during the pendancy of this appeal, the original claimant died on 13.07.2023 and his legal heirs are brought on record as appellants 2 to 4.
The learned counsel further submitted that though the Doctor assessed the disability of the original claimant as 35%, the Tribunal fixed the disability of the original claimant as 30%.

The learned counsel further submitted that the original claimant was in continuous treatment from the date of accident till his death and hence, the appellants 2 to 4 are entitled for compensation in respect of loss of love and affection and for consortium and further submitted https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis that the amount awarded for pain and sufferings and attender charges are also very meagre and hence, the appellants are entitled for enhancement in compensation.

The learned counsel further submitted that the award amount was already S.Manoharan (Died) vs A.Ganesh on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177597491/
2 withdrawn by the appellants.

sentences.text: 5.The learned counsel appearing for the second respondent Insurance Company submitted that the Tribunal after considering all the factual aspects, awarded the compensation which is just and reasonable and hence, the impugned judgment warrants no interference.

6.Heard the learned counsel appearing for the appellants claimants as well as the learned counsel appearing for the second respondent Insurance Company and perused the materials available on record.
7.The accident and the manner in which the accident happened are not disputed.
This appeal has been filed only questioning the quantum of compensation.
Hence, there is no need for any discussion with regard to negligence aspect.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis

8.The tribunal after elaborately discussing the factual aspects awarded a sum of Rs.40,000/- for pain and sufferings, Rs.40,000/- for extra nourishment and transport, Rs.90,000/- for disability,
Rs.36,000/- for loss of earnings or 3 months, Rs.5,000/- for medical expenses, Rs.40,000/- for loss of amenities, Rs.1,000/- for damages to clothes and Rs.9,600/- for attender charges and awarded a sum of Rs.2,61,600/- as compensation with interest at the rate of 7.5% p.a. from the date of numbering of petition i.e., 03.09.2014 till the date of realization.

9.Though the appellants 2 to 4 claim that the first appellant/ original claimant was in continuous treatment from the date of accident till his death, no medical records were produced before this Court to establish the same and hence their claim for loss of love and affection and consortium is not sustainable one.
10.The Tribunal after considering all the factual aspects, has awarded the compensation which is just and reasonable and hence, the impugned judgment warrants no interference.
It is represented t h a t t h e a w a r d a m o u n t w a s a l r e a d y w i t h d r a w n b y t h e a p p e l l a n t s a n d https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
hence, there is no need for this Court to make any apportionment.

M.DHANDAPANI,J.
pri 11.The civil miscellaneous appeal is dismissed.
The judgment and decree dated 02.03.2020 passed by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, V Court of Small Causes, Chennai, in M.C.O.P.No.5939 of 2014, is confirmed.
